suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-28 adds this relationship only as a bounded superior-canal-dehiscence auditory association. Superior semicircular canal dehiscence can present with conductive or pseudo-conductive hearing findings, but the diagnosis alone does not establish conductive hearing loss in every person or exclude other otologic causes. Require temporal-bone imaging interpreted with compatible symptoms, audiometry documenting the conductive phenotype, laterality and chronology, and otology review. Preserve otosclerosis, middle-ear disease, ossicular abnormalities, tympanic pathology, trauma, and mixed or sensorineural causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of superior semicircular canal dehiscence using appropriate high-resolution temporal-bone imaging
Formal audiometry defining conductive, pseudo-conductive, mixed, or sensorineural findings and laterality
Chronology of auditory symptoms, imaging, vestibular findings, and any surgical or treatment history
Assessment of otosclerosis, middle-ear or ossicular disease, tympanic pathology, trauma, and other hearing-loss causes
Otology or audiology assessment matching the imaging finding to the individual's functional hearing phenotype

sourceReferences.citation: Mikulec AA, McKenna MJ, Ramsey MJ, Rosowski JJ, Herrmann BS, Rauch SD, Curtin HD, Merchant SN. Superior semicircular canal dehiscence presenting as conductive hearing loss without vertigo. Otol Neurotol. 2004;25(2):121-129. PMID 15021770. doi:10.1097/00129492-200403000-00007.
sourceReferences.note: Clinical report describing superior semicircular canal dehiscence presenting with conductive hearing findings without vertigo. It supports a bounded phenotype association, not automatic individual attribution.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 15021770; reported conductive-hearing-loss phenotype without vertigo

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Superior semicircular canal dehiscence is reported with conductive or pseudo-conductive hearing findings, but a case-specific audiologic phenotype and exclusion of other otologic causes are required before any individual relationship is considered.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this clinical report; the mapping is not an individual otology opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A dehiscence may alter inner-ear sound and pressure transmission and produce an apparent conductive or pseudo-conductive audiometric pattern, but the mechanism and functional significance must be confirmed in the individual with imaging and audiology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Superior semicircular canal dehiscence can be accompanied by conductive-hearing findings, but the cited clinical report does not establish that every hearing deficit in a person with dehiscence is attributable to it; objective audiology, laterality, chronology, imaging, and competing-cause review are required.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent imaging and diagnosis; formal audiometry and laterality; chronology; otologic examination; review of otosclerosis, middle-ear, ossicular, tympanic, traumatic, mixed, and sensorineural alternatives; specialist assessment
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Chronic middle-ear disease, tympanic pathology, or trauma
Sensorineural, mixed, age-related, noise-related, or unrelated hearing loss
